title: What It Means When Prostate Cancer Spreads to Bone
hook: Joe Biden's cancer has reached his bones. An oncologist explains why bone is where prostate cancer usually goes — and why that isn't the end of the story.
key_points: Prostate cancer that spreads most often settles in bone.
Spread to bone means the disease is advanced, not that treatment stops.
Treatment shifts from cure to controlling the cancer and protecting quality of life.
Johns Hopkins oncologist Otis Brawley walked NPR through what the diagnosis means.
Many men live for years with advanced prostate cancer under treatment.
content_html: When news broke that former President Joe Biden's cancer had spread to his bones, NPR asked Johns Hopkins oncologist Otis Brawley to explain what that actually means. The short version: it's a serious turn, and it's also the most expected one.
extra_html:
Prostate cancer that leaves the prostate tends to head for bone. That pattern is common enough that unexplained bone pain in a man with a prostate cancer history is something doctors take seriously. Reaching bone means the disease is advanced — the aim of treatment moves from curing it to controlling it and protecting how well someone lives day to day.

That distinction gets lost in headlines, where "spread" reads as "over." Brawley's framing for NPR is more useful: advanced prostate cancer is a disease many men live with, under treatment, for years. The prevention lesson sits earlier in the story — knowing your own risk, and having the screening conversation with your doctor at the right age rather than after symptoms show up.

related.title: Prostate Health and Screening
related.hook: PSA screening for prostate cancer isn't an automatic yes. It's a genuine judgment call you make with your doctor.

related.title: Health Checks Men Skip
related.hook: Men see doctors less and die younger from preventable causes. A handful of simple checks catch the big risks early.

flashcards.prompt: Where does prostate cancer most commonly spread?
flashcards.explanation_html: Bone is the usual destination when prostate cancer spreads beyond the prostate — which is why bone pain can be a sign worth reporting.

flashcards.prompt: What changes about treatment once prostate cancer has spread to bone?
flashcards.back_html: The goal shifts from cure to control — holding the cancer back and protecting quality of life. Treatment continues; many men live for years with the disease managed.
